newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says Saudi crown prince to attend Tehran meet.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Saudi crown prince to attend Tehran meet.

text.p: Iran's official news agency IRNA said on Monday that Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Abdullah had told Iran's President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani he would attend an Islamic summit in Tehran in December.

It said Prince Abdullah told Rafsanjani at talks on Sunday in Islamabad on the sidelines of a summit of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) -- the world's largest Islamic body -- that he would attend the December OIC summit in Tehran.

If confirmed, the prince's visit to Tehran would be the first by a senior Saudi official to the Iranian capital in more than a decade of often tense relations between two of the world's largest oil exporters.
Saudi Arabia has not announced if it will attend the summit since King Fahd last week received an invitation from Rafsanjani delivered by Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati.
Velayati said his tour of the Gulf Arab states last week opened a new chapter in ties between Iran and its Arab neighbours across the Gulf.
Gulf Arab states have accused Iran of interfering in their internal affairs, a charge Iran denies, and voiced concern over its arms programme.
Riyadh has refused to confirm U.S. media reports of an Iranian link to a bombing that killed 19 U.S. servicemen in the eastern Saudi city of Khobar last June. Iran denies any role.
IRNA quoted Rafsanjani as saying after his talks with Prince Abdullah that he was "satisfied with the continuing efforts to improve relations with Saudi Arabia".
"He said both countries were willing to further improve ties and that cordial relations between the two countries will guarantee maintenance of security and stability in the region," IRNA said.

It said Rafsanjani condemned "those who would not like to see good relations between Iran and Saudi Arabia and added that these forces were trying to spoil mutual understanding and expansion of ties through disinformation", IRNA added.
"Both sides stressed the need for exchange of high-ranking officials...to achieve the goal of reconciliation and remove misunderstandings between the two Islamic neighbours," it said.
Iran says the United States accuses Tehran of being a threat in the region to justify continued American influence in the region as well as U.S. arms sales to the oil-rich states.
